what_it_does: NetTAG is a machine learning foundation model (like GPT but for chip design) trained to understand electronic circuits. Existing circuit representation methods require expensive symbolic computation (running full truth tables to verify logic) and work only on simple representations. NetTAG takes a different approach: it represents a circuit as a graph where each gate is a node annotated with its symbolic logic expression (AND, OR, NOT, etc.) and physical characteristics (size, delay, power). It uses an LLM to encode the symbolic gate descriptions into vectors, then a graph transformer to learn relationships between gates. The model trains on self-supervised objectives (predicting hidden nodes, reconstructing graphs) and aligns to both RTL (register-transfer level chip blueprints) and physical layout. Once trained, it can understand circuits at multiple design stages.
